description: Under the motto 'Abandoned, but never forgotten,' our team shares one mission: ensuring the sacrifices of the great aren't lost to the void. Through The Last Mission, we breathe life back into their stories, turning tragic ends into new legends. We guarantee that every hero who departed in silence will echo for eternity.
summary:
The "7 Ghosts" project is an interactive 3D web experience designed to solve a specific problem: the raw, complex, and dry nature of NASA's archive data. This project acts as a bridge between pure scientific data and the user, delivering an engaging, visually stunning, and 100% scientifically accurate journey.
​The experience begins with a hologram message emerging from the "Golden Record." This is followed by the gathering of seven "ghosts" (spacecraft) that form the number "7", alongside a terminal receiving a secret binary code. When you click on any shape, it reveals the hero's detailed story alongside an interactive 3D model. Once all seven heroes are explored, they merge into a circular ring to unlock their "Collective Testament." This message rolls like cinematic movie credits against a dark background, ultimately transitioning into a bright golden sunrise with a hopeful closing quote.

details:
NASA's archive is full of raw data, numbers, coordinates, and complex tables that are difficult for students and the general public to understand. Therefore, I designed my interactive website to act as a "bridge" between this raw data and the user, providing a smooth, enjoyable, and engaging experience.

The website consists of several scenes. The first page features an old, glitching screen losing its connection, which opens the gateway to the "Silent Archive." On the second page, the Voyager Golden Record appears at the bottom, projecting a holographic message on glass before prompting the user to click the "Awaken the 7 Ghosts" button.

The third page reveals 7 hexagonal shapes floating randomly for a few seconds before combining to form the number "7". Each shape has a short code made of the first two letters of the spacecraft's name and the last two digits of its launch year. On the left side, a terminal displays a secret binary code. When you click on any hexagon, the binary code disappears, revealing the spacecraft's story. At the top, you see an emotional title, the full name, and the launch year. At the bottom, a "View 3D Model" button expands to show a fully interactive 3D model, along with a close button to return to the story.

After exploring the personal archives, stories, and 3D models of all 7 spacecraft, the number "7" suddenly transforms into a rapidly spinning circle—mimicking electrons orbiting the nucleus of an RTG nuclear reactor, which powers most of these missions. A button appears in the center to open their final "Collective Testament."

This opens the fourth page, where cinematic credits slowly roll up the middle of the screen against a very dark background. Once the credits finish rolling, the background suddenly changes into a bright golden color, accompanied by a final quote of optimism.

Technical Details & Resources:

The code was written using HTML, CSS, and JS. I also used the <model-viewer> library, developed by Google, to display the 3D models smoothly and allow the user to easily rotate and interact with them.

The project features 7 spacecraft: Opportunity, Kepler, Cassini, Perseverance, Voyager, Curiosity, and New Horizons. To fulfill the hackathon's requirement of using at least one NASA resource, I utilized two official resources: Kepler and Opportunity.

To guarantee 100% scientific accuracy, all data, texts, and 3D shapes were sourced directly from NASA's official website and archives. Finally, AI tools like Gemini and Claude were used to assist me throughout the development of this project.
